A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Outlier-Robust Diffusion Solvers for Inverse Problems. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison. All eight appendix pages render identically after matching their shifted page positions.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original reconstruction experiments on CelebA, ImageNet and FFHQ, including benchmark comparisons, robustness tests, ablations and computational-cost analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same noise estimation, Huber/IRLS objective, gradient-descent updates and conjugate-gradient procedure with finite-difference approximation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CelebA, ImageNet and FFHQ on 4× super-resolution, random 70% inpainting, Gaussian deblurring, motion deblurring and nonlinear deblurring. The outlier-contamination and high-Gaussian-noise scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding linear comparisons retain DPS, DiffPIR, DCPS, RED-diff and DAPS; nonlinear comparisons retain DPS, RED-diff and DAPS. Appendix B.4 retains Robust-DPS and Robust-DiffPIR. The newly cited Yang et al. work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported 100-image samples, 256×256 resolution, degradation settings, contamination fractions, noise levels and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Algorithm budgets and hyperparameters in Table 7 also match.

E4.justification: The high-noise test, Huber-threshold and finite-difference sensitivity studies, learning-rate and conjugate-term ablations, component comparisons and efficiency analysis are retained unchanged in Sections 4.4–4.5 and Appendix B.3–B.4.

E5.justification: Tables 1–3 and 8–9 retain the same ± reporting. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation explanation, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in result Tables 1–6 and 8–13 match, including benchmark, ablation and component-comparison results. The reconstruction examples and computational-cost plots also match; no result is added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The corruption model, diffusion equations, Huber/IRLS definitions and conjugate-gradient derivations in Equations 1–26 are unchanged. No formal assumption, mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2 and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about outlier robustness, reconstruction performance and avoiding delicate learning-rate tuning. The added code-access sentence does not change the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of noise refinement, Huber robustness and learning-rate sensitivity, together with interpretations of the ablations and efficiency tradeoff, remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code-availability statement and a specific Robust-DAPS repository address in the abstract, absent from v1. Existing hardware and hyperparameter documentation remains unchanged. The PDFs establish the access-information addition, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Yang et al., Outlier-robust diffusion posterior sampling for bayesian inverse problems, as reference [68]. This is a limited citation addition without substantive comparative discussion; the existing positioning, including Appendix A's IRLS-PnPDP discussion, is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code-access sentence, with accompanying citation and version-text updates. The existing prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page reflow relocates existing material: Figure 3 moves from PDF page 6 to page 7, and Tables 5–6 shift within page 8. Figures and tables retain their content, designs and captions; the appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The new implementation address improves code discoverability, and the added related-work citation modestly improves attribution. These are limited documentation gains; the scientific content and appendices remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish whether the linked implementation is complete or executable.
